# The Twist Map and the One-to-One Correspondence

Let $G = \operatorname{Gal}(k^{\mathrm{al}}/k)$ and fix an elliptic curve $E_0/k$. We classify $k$-forms (twists) of $E_0$, i.e. elliptic curves $E/k$ with $E \otimes_k k^{\mathrm{al}} \cong E_0 \otimes_k k^{\mathrm{al}}$, up to $k$-isomorphism.

## The map $E \mapsto [\alpha]$

Given a twist $E/k$ together with a choice of $k^{\mathrm{al}}$-isomorphism $\varphi : E_0 \to E$, define for each $\sigma \in G$
$$
\alpha_\sigma \;=\; \varphi^{-1} \circ \sigma(\varphi) \;\in\; \operatorname{Aut}_{k^{\mathrm{al}}}(E_0),
$$
where $\sigma(\varphi) = \sigma \circ \varphi \circ \sigma^{-1}$ is the morphism obtained by applying $\sigma$ to the coefficients/graph of $\varphi$.

**Cocycle identity.** Since $\sigma(\varphi) = \varphi \circ \alpha_\sigma$ by definition, applying $\sigma$ to $\tau(\varphi)=\varphi\circ\alpha_\tau$ gives
$$
(\sigma\tau)(\varphi)=\sigma(\varphi)\circ\sigma(\alpha_\tau)=\varphi\circ\alpha_\sigma\circ\sigma(\alpha_\tau).
$$
But also $(\sigma\tau)(\varphi)=\varphi\circ\alpha_{\sigma\tau}$, hence
$$
\alpha_{\sigma\tau}=\alpha_\sigma\circ\sigma(\alpha_\tau),
$$
so $\alpha$ is a $1$-cocycle $G\to\operatorname{Aut}_{k^{\mathrm{al}}}(E_0)$.

**Independence of $\varphi$.** If $\psi:E_0\to E$ is another choice, set $\beta=\psi^{-1}\circ\varphi\in\operatorname{Aut}_{k^{\mathrm{al}}}(E_0)$. The cocycle $\alpha'$ built from $\psi$ satisfies $\psi\circ\alpha'_\sigma=\sigma(\psi)$, while $\varphi=\psi\circ\beta$ gives
$$
\sigma(\varphi)=\sigma(\psi)\circ\sigma(\beta)=\psi\circ\alpha'_\sigma\circ\sigma(\beta)=\varphi\circ\beta^{-1}\circ\alpha'_\sigma\circ\sigma(\beta).
$$
Comparing with $\sigma(\varphi)=\varphi\circ\alpha_\sigma$ yields $\alpha_\sigma=\beta^{-1}\circ\alpha'_\sigma\circ\sigma(\beta)$, i.e. $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ are cohomologous. Thus the class
$$
[\alpha]\in H^1\!\bigl(G,\operatorname{Aut}_{k^{\mathrm{al}}}(E_0)\bigr)
$$
depends only on the $k$-isomorphism class of $E$.

## The inverse map $[\alpha]\mapsto E$

Given a cocycle $\alpha:G\to\operatorname{Aut}_{k^{\mathrm{al}}}(E_0)$, define a **twisted Galois action** on $E_0(k^{\mathrm{al}})$ by
$$
\sigma * P \;=\; \alpha_\sigma\bigl(\sigma(P)\bigr).
$$
The cocycle identity guarantees this is a genuine $G$-action:
$$
(\sigma\tau)*P=\alpha_{\sigma\tau}(\sigma\tau(P))=\alpha_\sigma\sigma(\alpha_\tau)\sigma(\tau(P))=\alpha_\sigma(\sigma(\alpha_\tau(\tau(P))))=\sigma*(\tau*P).
$$
By **Galois descent** (Weil's descent theorem, equivalently fppf descent for the quasi-projective variety $E_0$), the fixed locus
$$
E \;=\; \bigl(E_0,\, *\text{-action}\bigr)^{G}
$$
is an elliptic curve over $k$ with $E\otimes_k k^{\mathrm{al}}\cong E_0$, and the identity map $\varphi:E_0\to E\otimes k^{\mathrm{al}}$ recovers the cocycle $\alpha_\sigma=\varphi^{-1}\circ\sigma(\varphi)$. A cohomologous cocycle $\alpha'_\sigma=\beta^{-1}\alpha_\sigma\sigma(\beta)$ produces the same $k$-isomorphism class (the descent differs by the $k^{\mathrm{al}}$-automorphism $\beta$ of $E_0$, which is absorbed in the descent datum). Hence the construction descends to a well-defined map on cohomology classes.

## The two maps are inverse

- Starting from $E$, descending via the cocycle $\alpha_\sigma=\varphi^{-1}\sigma(\varphi)$ and then taking the identity $\varphi$ as the comparison isomorphism returns $E$ itself.
- Starting from $[\alpha]$, the descent $E$ comes equipped with the identity $E_0\to E\otimes k^{\mathrm{al}}$, whose associated cocycle is exactly $\alpha$.

Therefore the assignment
$$
\boxed{\;\bigl\{k\text{-twists of }E_0\bigr\}/\cong_k \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; H^1\!\bigl(\operatorname{Gal}(k^{\mathrm{al}}/k),\,\operatorname{Aut}_{k^{\mathrm{al}}}(E_0)\bigr)\;}
$$
is a **one-to-one correspondence**. The forward direction sends $(E,\varphi)$ to the class of the cocycle $\sigma\mapsto\varphi^{-1}\sigma(\varphi)$; the inverse direction sends a cocycle class to the Galois descent of $E_0$ along the twisted action $\sigma*=\alpha_\sigma\circ\sigma$. Injectivity is precisely the statement that cohomologous cocycles yield $k$-isomorphic twists, and surjectivity is Weil's descent theorem.
